absent: Remainder of load_elf_binary after the truncated PIE handling discussion, including bias selection, segment install, and process entry setup.
Numeric values and full layouts for auxiliary tags, ELF headers, program entries, notes, properties, and binprm fields.
Locking, lifetime, and error behavior of interpreter files, memory mappings, and argument page setup beyond what is shown.
Architecture-specific ELF validation, property handling, personality, and stack-top behavior beyond default allow hooks.

findings.text: Main ELF binary loader validates identity type and architecture, loads program headers, resolves an interpreter when present, consults property and architecture hooks, replaces the execution context, prepares argument pages, then maps loadable segments with calculated bias and permissions.

Binary loading advances through identification checks, optional interpreter path extraction and header fetch, stack permission and processor header scan, interpreter validation, property and architecture approval, context replacement and argument setup, then ordered segment mapping with first-load placement handling.

Stack setup publishes optional platform and execution descriptors into saved auxiliary state terminated by a zero entry, reserves room for counts and vectors, positions the stack base according to growth direction, extends the mapping, then records argument and environment pointer lists followed by auxiliary data.

Stack preparation aborts when address extension is unavailable, when storing counts or pointers or copying auxiliary data faults, or when measured argument or environment strings are empty or exceed the per-string limit.

Stack extension holds the address space write lock in killable mode only across lookup or extension of the mapping covering the argument position, then releases it before user memory stores; interruption aborts preparation.
Auxiliary flags derivation prefers transparent interpreter mode over preserve initial argument mode when both indicators are set, otherwise reports no flags.

Segment file mapping aligns offset and length to page boundaries, returns the aligned address without mapping for empty size, reserves the whole image when a total size is supplied then releases the tail beyond the current segment, and reports collisions when fixed no-replace placement meets an existing mapping.

Loadable segment handling maps file-backed content when present, clears the tail of the final file page, and allocates anonymous zero pages where memory size exceeds file size while honoring requested execute permission for that tail; purely anonymous segments use the aligned address as base.
Total span computation considers only loadable entries, tracking the lowest page start and highest segment end; it yields zero when no loadable entry exists.
Small ELF metadata reads require the full requested byte count; short reads become input-output errors while underlying negative status is preserved.
Kernel read service first validates the requested range against file and position, then delegates to a synchronous vector implementation shared by in-kernel file readers.

Synchronous kernel vector read clamps length, requires read mode and read capability, rejects unsupported operation wiring, uses the supplied position or zero, updates position and access accounting only on positive transfer, and always counts the attempt.
Unsupported kernel file operation helper emits a rate-limited diagnostic identifying operation file process and command name and reports invalid argument.
Alignment selection scans only loadable entries, ignores non-power-of-two values, retains the largest valid alignment, and finally rounds up to at least page granularity.

Program header loading rejects unexpected entry size and empty or oversized table byte size, allocates kernel memory for the table, reads it from the recorded file offset, and frees and reports absence on any failure.
Architecture ELF state is an empty carrier with an empty initializer, providing a hook placeholder with no stored fields in this configuration.
Default architecture hooks for processor-specific entries, whole-image validation, protection adjustment, and property parsing unconditionally permit progress without inspecting inputs.
Segment protection derivation maps readable writable and executable segment flags to corresponding memory protections, then passes the result through architecture adjustment.

Interpreter loading accepts only executable or dynamic types with suitable architecture and mappability, requires a non-empty loadable span, maps each loadable entry with interpreter-context protections using fixed placement after the first decision or bias compensation for dynamic images, derives load bias from the first mapping, and validates address overflow size ordering and task limits.

Property entry parsing bounds-checks offsets alignment and descriptor lengths, enforces strictly increasing property types, delegates each entry to architecture handling, and ends successfully only on exhaustion; the container parser limits note size, checks note type name and descriptor extents, and skips work when the feature is disabled or no property header is present.

Malformed header tables, unterminated interpreter path, oversized property notes, misaligned or truncated property records, unsorted property types, and interpreter address overflow or size inversion abort loading with format or memory errors.

Observed ABI facts include auxiliary tags for executable path platform base platform descriptor and restart-sequence sizing and alignment, program types for load interpreter stack and GNU property plus a processor range, segment permission bits for read write execute, object types for executable and dynamic files, and a one kilobyte property note buffer with GNU property naming.
